Introduction
Founded in Paris in 1961 by André and Coqueline Courrèges, Courrèges redeﬁned femininity by 
liberating women from the restrictive silhouettes of the 1950s.
•
Inﬂuenced by André Courrèges’ early work at Balenciaga, the brand introduced 
architectural precision, geometric silhouettes, and technical materials.
•
A deﬁning force of the 1960s Space Age, Courrèges brought futurism into haute couture 
through miniskirts, A-line shapes, and iconic white peep-toe  ankle boots.
•
Under Artistic Director Nicolas Di Felice (joined 2020), the house reinterprets its heritage 
through sleek minimalism, sensuality, and modern wearability all while upholding an ethical 
standard to the environment. Recent collections, including Blinded by the Sun, use global warming 
as a metaphor to push ideas of melting, exposure, and extremity while maintaining core brand 
codes.
•
From early Space Race–inspired campaigns such as Moon Girl to today, Courrèges 
continues to balance innovation, ethics, and aesthetics in a contemporary context.

Brand Leadership
●
Founded in 1961 by André Courrèges and 
Coqueline Courrèges. iconic creative leadership 
deﬁned the brand’s futuristic identity early on
●
The business faced instability through the 
1980s–2010s, changing owners & struggling to 
remain relevant
●
In 2018, luxury holding Artemis (Pinault family) 
became full owner, bringing stronger business 
strategy and investment to the house
●
Creative leadership became more strategic: 
Nicolas Di Felice was appointed Creative Director 
in Sept 2020, bringing fresh vision and revitalizing 
the brand’s identity while aligning with business 
goals
●
Di Felice’s work reinterprets Courrèges’ the 
brand’s original futuristic look in ways that 
resonate with modern consumers and fashion 
markets (minimalism, club inﬂuences, structural 
innovation)
●
Recently (2024), Marie Leblanc was appointed 
CEO, signaling a stronger business leadership 
focus alongside creative direction to grow both 
revenue and brand relevance
●
Today the business & creative sides collaborate 
closely, balancing heritage with innovation and 
commercial strategy

Controversies
-
1960s redeﬁning women’s fashion
-
Power suit
-
Trousers
-
Miniskirt invention
-
Controversy over whether Andre Courreges invented it or Mary Quant
-
Courreges ﬁrst to make over-the-knee skirt but Mary Quant marketed it
-
Hiatus from 1965 to 1966
-
Courreges didn’t like that his “Space Age” collection was being copied for cheap
-
Declined to do a fall 1965 show that led to a hiatus until 1967
-
Resulted in him creating more affordable, ready-to-wear pieces to put an end to the 
copies
-
Couture Future
-
Felt that Haute Couture was becoming unrealistic stylistically and economically
-
Created ready to wear line called “Couture Future”
-
Leadership turnover 2010s -> public uncertainty regarding Courreges 
stability
-
2011- bought by Jacques Bungert and Frederic Torloting
-
Sébastien Meyer and Arnaud Vaillant only lasted for 2 years (2015-2017)
-
2016- Andre Courreges dies
-
2018- Artemis takes full control
-
Christina Ahlers and Yolanda Zobel also only 2 years (2018-2020)

Assessment
-
Current Creative Director: Nicolas Di Felice
-
Strong mix of commercial background from Balenciaga, Dior, LV
-
Heritage x Modernity
-
Continues “Space Age” minimalism
-
Still feels contemporary and relevant
-
Turning archival pieces into something wearable and desirable
-
Campaigns
-
FW25 Confetti blocks model silhouettes to push a light, fun experience 
-
Spring 2026- models shot the pre-collections in the streets of Paris using 
mirrors around the city
-
New Valentine’s Day digital campaign, Togetherness, highlights closeness 
-
Photographs of simple interactions between models with little 
distraction
-
“Meaning through relationships rather than spectacle”
-
Audience and market
-
Targeting younger audiences who appreciate social media, more accessible 
pricing, and experiential designs
-
Success
-
4 new boutiques in Korea in the last 18 months
-
Doubled annual revenues in recent years
-
Expected to continue growing with success of recent creative director and 
continuation of sparking conversations and making statements
